liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Attics Of My Life** (1 review): Reviewer finds Attics a real beauty, especially for the period [11]
- **Dancin In The Streets (splendid version)** (1 review): Reviewer calls the ending Dancing off the charts [11]
- **Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer's copy has complete Dancing in the Streets and Lovelight, followed by an Uncle John's Band encore [12]
- **jam** (1 review): Reviewer labeled the first set Acoustic Pigpen and is puzzled by the purpose of track 18, listed as jam [16]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): Cryptical Envelopment goes into Drums and The Other One, then Me & My Uncle, back to The Other One, then Dancin' In The Streets [1]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 other source): Cryptical Envelopment leads into Drums and The Other One, with Me & My Uncle in the middle, ending with Dancin' In The Streets [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **So Sad (To Watch Good Love Go Bad)**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [18]
- **A Voice From On High**: rare: 5 archived performances [18]
- **Swing Low, Sweet Chariot**: rare: 13 archived performances [18]
- **Six Days On The Road**: rare: 13 archived performances [18]
- **Truck Drivin' Man**: rare: 14 archived performances [18]
- **Dirty Business**: rare: 12 archived performances [18]
- **Lodi**: rare: 12 archived performances [18]
- **Only Daddy That'll Walk The Line**: rare: 3 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-07-12.aud.composite.130938.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 36 songs; 200 min [1]
- **gd1970-07-12.aud.mysteryreel.cloverman.smith.GEMS.108002.flac16**: audience recording; 31 songs; 158 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the sound a definite C, though the show outweighs that [11]
- **gd1970-07-12.aud.unknown.sirmick.24663.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 31 songs; 163 min; rated 4.08/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience tape with some hand clapping; it sounds as if recorded from the lobby or audience area; Sound is hard to hear in places and hard to listen to in others; Reviewer thinks the tape runs noticeably slow and could be sped up [3][6][15][17]
- **gd1970-07-12.aud.cooper.122707.flac16**: audience recording; 30 songs; 142 min [4]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Night Of The Living Dead" [1]
- Reviewer believes this is most likely the July 11 show, not July 12 [7]
- Reviewer bought a first Dead bootleg outside the Fillmore East while Bill Graham shouted at the crowd to stay in line [10]
- Reviewer attended both the 11th and 12th and says the dates are swapped; this is really July 11 [13]
- Reviewer says the tape holds mostly New Riders material and very little Grateful Dead [14]
- Reviewer finds the acoustic set especially sweet [15]
- Midnight show billed as Grateful Dead and New Riders; the first set was acoustic [1]
- These were midnight shows, so dates confuse historians: concerts are listed under one day but occur the next [2]
- Reviewer suggests comparing this show's Me And My Uncle with the previous night's to hear the speed difference [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-07-12.aud.composite.130938.flac16**: transferred by Rob Darst;Jim Cooper;Jim Cotsman; source: Combination of the two audience recordings shnid 9379 and shnid 122707; edits were limited to volume, speed, cross-fades at the beginning and end of patches,… [1]
- **gd1970-07-12.aud.mysteryreel.cloverman.smith.GEMS.108002.flac16**: taped by Mystery Reel of an unknown audience recording uncovered  and shared by LL member Cloverman, which he sent to Matt Smith for his great reel transfer work.  The handwriting on the reel case is thought to be Latvala's, no more is known.; transferred by edited and mastered by Jamie Waddell with listening assistance by Jim Blackwood. Rel transfer by Matt Smith; source: unknown audience recording [2]
- **gd1970-07-12.aud.unknown.sirmick.24663.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by SirMick; source: aud > ??? > shn > wav > shn [3]. Also: Taper apparently paused the recorder often, leaving small cuts between most tracks; some track starts and ends are missing; Transferrer balanced fluctuating channel volumes where possible and patched dropouts using the other channel [3]
- **gd1970-07-12.aud.cooper.122707.flac16**: taped by Jim Cooper; source: Jim Cooper's Hitachi TRQ-222 Cassette recording > CDR > WAV > FLAC [4]
